5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 2

Past simple: regular verbs

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about finished actions with regular verbs (acciones terminadas)
  • Write the -ed ending with the correct spelling
  • Pronounce -ed in three ways: /t/, /d/ and /ɪd/
  • Make negatives and questions with didn't and did

Para pensar

Hoy I play al fútbol. Ayer… ¿cómo se dice «jugué»?

Explicación

Finished actions

We use the past simple to talk about actions that started and finished in the past: «Yesterday I cleaned my room», «Last Saturday we visited the zoo», «In 2023 my family moved to Valencia».

The action is over: it is not happening now. That's why we usually say when it happened: yesterday, last night, last week, three days ago, in 2022. En castellano: equivale a «limpié», «visitamos», «se mudó». Y una gran ventaja: el verbo inglés no cambia con la persona: I walked, you walked, he walked, we walked.

The rule: add -ed

Most verbs are regular. To make the past, we just add -ed: walk → walked, play → played, watch → watched, help → helped, cook → cooked, start → started, open → opened, jump → jumped.

It's the same for all persons: «I listened», «She listened», «They listened». We don't add -s for he or she in the past. Compare: «She plays the piano every day» (present) and «She played the piano yesterday» (past).

Spelling: -d, -ied and double letters

Some verbs need a little change. 1. Verbs ending in -e add only -d: like → liked, dance → danced, live → lived, arrive → arrived.

2. Consonant + y changes to -ied: study → studied, carry → carried, try → tried. But vowel + y just adds -ed: play → played, enjoy → enjoyed. 3. Short verbs ending in consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter: stop → stopped, plan → planned, hug → hugged, drop → dropped.

Three ways to say -ed

The ending -ed doesn't always sound the same. It has three sounds. /t/ after sounds like p, k, s, sh, ch, f: walked («uokt»), jumped, washed, laughed. /d/ after most other sounds: played («pleid»), opened, cleaned, lived.

/ɪd/ only after t or d, and then it adds a new syllable: wanted («uón-tid»), started, needed, decided. En castellano: el error más típico es pronunciar «-ed» entero siempre: «uók-ed». Solo se dice así cuando el verbo acaba en t o d.

Negatives with didn't

For the negative we use didn't (did not) + the verb without -ed. «I didn't watch TV.» «He didn't play in the match.» «We didn't finish the puzzle.»

Why without -ed? Because did already tells us it's the past, so the verb goes back to its basic form. Never say «I didn't watched». En castellano: es como en el presente con don't y doesn't: el auxiliar se lleva el tiempo y el verbo queda «limpio».

Questions with did

For questions, put Did at the start + subject + verb without -ed: «Did you enjoy the party?» «Did she call you?» Short answers: «Yes, I did.» «No, she didn't.»

With question words: «What did you cook?» «Where did they travel?» «When did the film start?» Ojo: no confundas con was/were: para el verbo to be no usamos did («Were you tired?»), pero para el resto de verbos, sí («Did you walk?»).

Sequencing words

When we tell a story in the past, we use sequencing words to put the actions in order: First (primero), Then (luego), Next (después), After that (después de eso) and Finally (por último).

«First, I washed my face. Then, I brushed my teeth. After that, I prepared my bag. Finally, I walked to school.» These words make your text clear and easy to follow. Use a comma after them when they start the sentence.

Reading: a rainy Saturday

Read Nora's text: «Last Saturday it rained all day, so I stayed at home. First, I helped my dad in the kitchen. We baked a carrot cake and it smelled great! Then, I tidied my room and I discovered an old board game under the bed. After that, my brother and I played it for two hours. He laughed a lot because I lost every time. In the evening we watched a film and we chatted with my cousins on the computer. I didn't open my books, but I enjoyed the day.»

Find ten regular verbs. Which ones have /ɪd/? Which verb is in the negative?

Let's practise: what did you do?

Play «Find someone who…». Walk around the class and ask: «Did you watch a film last weekend?» «Did you visit your grandparents?» «Did you cook something?» When someone says «Yes, I did», write their name.

Then write a short report: «Lola watched a film. Max visited his grandparents. Nobody cooked.» Repaso: + -ed en afirmativa; didn't + verbo sin -ed en negativa; Did…? + verbo sin -ed en pregunta.

Regular verbs

Ejercicios

  1. Write the past: clean, love, carry, plan.

  2. Complete: «Yesterday we ___ (visit) the castle.»

  3. Complete: «My cat ___ (jump) on the table.»

  4. Make it negative: «I studied for the test.»

  5. Make a question: «You listened to the radio.»

  6. Answer: «Did your team play well?» (yes)

  7. Classify by sound /t/, /d/, /ɪd/: needed, washed, opened.

  8. Correct: «We stoped at the shop and walkt home.»

  9. Order: «didn't / he / the / tidy / room»

  10. Write four sentences about yesterday with First, Then, After that, Finally.

Practica

  1. The past of «watch» is…

    1. A) watcht
    2. B) watchied
    3. C) watched

  2. The past of «like» is…

    1. A) liked
    2. B) likeed
    3. C) likied

  3. The past of «study» is…

    1. A) studyed
    2. B) studied
    3. C) studed

  4. The past of «play» is…

    1. A) plaied
    2. B) played
    3. C) playd

  5. The past of «stop» is…

    1. A) stoped
    2. B) stopt
    3. C) stopped

  6. «She didn't ___ the window.»

    1. A) open
    2. B) opened
    3. C) opens

  7. «___ you help your dad?»

    1. A) Do
    2. B) Were
    3. C) Did

  8. In «wanted», -ed sounds…

    1. A) /t/
    2. B) /ɪd/
    3. C) /d/

  9. In «jumped», -ed sounds…

    1. A) /t/
    2. B) /ɪd/
    3. C) /d/

  10. Which word puts actions in order?

    1. A) Then
    2. B) Yesterday
    3. C) Because

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el pasado simple; Cómo se forma el pasado de un verbo regular y sus reglas de ortografía; Cómo se pronuncia la terminación -ed; Cómo se hacen negativas y preguntas con did.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

Regular verbHace el pasado con -ed.
-e → -dlike → liked.
consonante + y → -iedstudy → studied.
doble consonantestop → stopped.
/t/ /d/ /ɪd/walked · played · wanted.
didn't + verboI didn't play.
Did…?Did you play? Yes, I did.
First, then, finallyOrdenan lo que pasó.

Soluciones

  1. C) Regla general: + -ed.
  2. A) Acaba en -e: + d.
  3. B) Consonante + y → -ied.
  4. B) Vocal + y: + ed.
  5. C) Se dobla la consonante.
  6. A) Tras didn't, sin -ed.
  7. C) Pregunta en pasado: Did.
  8. B) Tras t: sílaba nueva.
  9. A) Tras p: /t/.
  10. A) Then = luego.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. cleaned, loved, carried, planned.
  2. visited.
  3. jumped.
  4. I didn't study for the test.
  5. Did you listen to the radio?
  6. Yes, it did. / Yes, they did.
  7. needed /ɪd/, washed /t/, opened /d/.
  8. We stopped at the shop and walked home.
  9. He didn't tidy the room.
  10. Model answer: First, I walked to school. Then, I played with my friends. After that, I helped my mum. Finally, I watched TV.
